clue.text: Interrupt study on source of bacteria and eat

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: to interrupt is to break into something

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to study a subject at university is to read it

explanation.surface: Someone stops studying a germ culture to have a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking bread is an idiom for sharing a meal, so it stands for eating together.

clue.text: Responsibility for cash in America

definitions.meaning: as in 'the ... stops here', the duty that gets passed along

explanation.surface: Someone is accountable for money held in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing the buck shifts the duty; in US slang a buck is a dollar, hence cash.

clue.text: Act married after misrepresentation of real rank

indicators.note: the act and married pieces come after the rearranged letters
misrepresenting the word real gives its letters a false new arrangement

parts.note: to act is to do

explanation.surface: A marriage ceremony follows a false claim about someone's true status.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank or title held by a nobleman of that grade.

clue.text: Bounder to seek trial here?

parts.note: an animal that bounds along, here the leaping marsupial rather than a cad
to court something, as danger or favour, is to seek it

explanation.surface: A cad goes looking for a hearing in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like the old word for a scoundrel; it is literally something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for an irregular, unfair tribunal, a place where a sham trial is held.

clue.text: Decay rampant and in American buildings

parts.note: rot means decay

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the abbreviation for American
rampant suggests unruly wildness, so these letters run riot

explanation.surface: Rot is spreading through buildings in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampant' scrambles AND into NDA, which goes 'in' US.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, usually domed, so the plural means such buildings.

clue.text: Garment from India prone to be revealing

indicators.note: the words India prone reveal a run of letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A garment from India is apt to be skimpy.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a protective garment tied over the front of one's clothes.

clue.text: Result of injury that's almost frightening

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: frightening means scary

explanation.surface: An injury left something nearly terrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: Cut short story aired in support of dog

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: aired means spoken out, so the word for story is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A short story is broadcast to back up a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail something is to reduce or abbreviate it.

clue.text: Dire scenes played out in such homes

indicators.note: the words are acted out in a new arrangement, as a scene is staged

explanation.surface: Grim dramas are staged in certain houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Residences are dwellings, the places where people live.

clue.text: Singer backed by company offering headgear

indicators.note: by means the company piece stands beside the reversed singer
backed means the singer's word is read back to front

parts.note: a tenor is a male singer

explanation.surface: A vocalist with corporate backing offers a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown, a piece of ceremonial headwear.

clue.text: Places haunted by engineer types?

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
types are sorts

explanation.surface: Places supposedly visited by engineering kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Resorts are places people frequent, a haunt being somewhere often visited.

clue.text: Confirms advance on stint at sea fighting

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages

indicators.note: fighting suggests a scuffle that throws the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A payment is promised for a period of naval combat.
explanation.definitionFit: To substantiate a claim is to back it with evidence, verifying it.

clue.text: Part of kitchen sapping poet full of love

parts.note: sapping means draining

indicators.note: the poet holds the letter for love inside

parts.note: a bard is a poet
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: An exhausting poet who is besotted is part of the household.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the grooved surface beside a sink where washed dishes drip dry.

clue.text: What man's partner may be? Protest he must be upset about origin of money

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the money letter
upset means the words protest he are knocked into a new arrangement
the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A protester is angry over where money came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's wife may be the parent-by-marriage of his children from an earlier union.

clue.text: The heartless member has spoken of such lords

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word is removed, leaving the ends

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
spoken means oral

explanation.surface: A callous parliamentarian has talked about certain peers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lords Temporal are the non-bishop members of the UK House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers who sit by secular title rather than as bishops are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Hot line in forged notes

indicators.note: the line letter goes inside the reworked letters
forged means faked, so the word notes is remade

explanation.surface: A tip-off about counterfeit banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen goods, as in a hot car.

clue.text: Excited, as to come out

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled at the prospect of coming out.
explanation.definitionFit: Out can mean unconscious, knocked out cold, as in a deep coma.

clue.text: Wages must cover most of crowd in Rome office

indicators.note: the wages word wraps around the shortened crowd word

parts.note: wages are pay

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a crowd is a pack

explanation.surface: Pay must be stretched to include most of a crowd in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office of Pope, based in Rome.

clue.text: Cream were first to get drunk

parts.note: the cream of a group is the pick, the best
led means went first, were in front

explanation.surface: The cream got there first to become sozzled.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is informal for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Disadvantage of drink with team?

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Is there a drawback to drinking with the team?
explanation.definitionFit: A downside is a negative aspect or drawback.

clue.text: Taking some despite miserable list

indicators.note: Taking some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone takes a share despite a wretched inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out item by item, enumerating.

clue.text: How to start a childhood romance?

definitions.text: How to start a childhood romance?

parts.words: How to start a childhood romance?
parts.note: the romance is a fairy story for children, and this is its traditional opening line, not a first love

explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' suggests young love; it is a tale, and the clue asks for the stock opening words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales classically open with this phrase, which begins a children's story.

clue.text: Monsters turn up with Dr Seuss regularly

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for turn is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Dr Seuss stories routinely feature beasts popping up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GO to OG; 'regularly' takes R, E, S from Dr Seuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore.

clue.text: Worst gamble accommodating son

indicators.note: the gamble word makes room for the son letter inside

parts.note: a gamble is a bet

explanation.surface: The worst wager ever included a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' is a verb here: to worst someone is to defeat them.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to worst and to best both mean to defeat an opponent.

clue.text: Those worried about left and right keep arm in this

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the left letter
worried means agitated, so the word those is jumbled

explanation.surface: Anxious people on both sides of politics keep a weapon handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns THOSE into HOSTE, which goes 'about' L, with R added after.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is the case worn on a belt to carry a pistol, the arm.

clue.text: Tedious working alfresco

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Dull work done in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco means in the open air, not indoors.

clue.text: Free, free at last to travel

parts.note: to free of something is to rid

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the second free

explanation.surface: Finally liberated and able to journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel on a horse, bike or vehicle.

clue.text: Evaluation of agreement covering awful mess

indicators.note: the agreement word goes over and around the jumbled letters

parts.note: assent is agreement

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, so the word mess is wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A report on a deal that papers over a terrible mess.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a judgement of value or quality, an appraisal.
